items.title: paperclipai/paperclip
items.contentSnippet:
The open-source app everyone uses to manage agents at work

  
 
 Quickstart · Docs · GitHub · Discord · Twitter · Website 
 
     
 
 
 
  
 
 
Paperclip is the app people use to manage AI agents for work.
 
Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents.
 
If OpenClaw is an employee, Paperclip is the company.
 
Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business. Bring your own agents, assign goals, and track work and costs from one dashboard.

items.title: Show HN: NiceShot AI – The analytics layer competitive games forgot to add
items.contentSnippet:
I've been working on NiceShot AI for the last 26 months as a way to experiment with computer vision for gameplay analysis.
The basic idea is to take a recorded long gameplay session and automatically turn it into structured gameplay information and highlights. Bridging the performance analysis gap between match stats (too short) & lifetime stats (too long).
The current pipeline is:
Gameplay video → YOLO detection → event tracking → OCR/context filtering → event timestamps → clips → highlight com

items.title: Show HN: Sketchling – a hand-drawn animation language for coding agents
items.contentSnippet:
I built sketchling this weekend to see if agents can draw something that looks natural and hand-drawn if given the right primitives. This was inspired by Manim after watching how powerful an agent-native way to produce animations can be.
It is a small typescript library with shapes that take character parameters like weight, looseness, and energy. It renders through rough.js and GSAP through a headless chromium browser. It has tools like a built-in linter and is meant to be agent-native.

items.title: Show HN: Airship – Figma-Like Visual Editor for Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode
items.contentSnippet:
I wanted to experiment with my UI like I do in Figma, without having to rebuild it in a separate design tool. So I built Airship.
It lets you prototype directly in your running app, select elements, make changes, and explore different directions visually.
Once you like something, Airship applies the changes to your source. No mockups to keep in sync, or bouncing back and forth between design and code.
